title: Workforce joiner, mover and leaver lifecycle
status_rationale: No workforce identity provider, HR system or provisioning process was located. Headcount is not established. SOC2-010 requires provisioning and deprovisioning coverage as a design directive only.
target_answer: All workforce access derives from a single authoritative identity provider tied to an engagement record (employee or contractor, with end date). Access is granted only through approved role bundles; there is no direct grant on target systems. Termination disables the identity provider account immediately (same business day for voluntary departures, immediately for involuntary), which cascades through federation to every connected system; systems that cannot federate are listed and deprovisioned by an automated task with evidence. Role changes revoke old access before new access is granted. Dormant accounts are disabled after a defined inactivity period. A daily match of identity-provider administrative actions against approved requests detects unapproved grants (TVR-SEC-008).
intended_practice: Select a workforce identity provider before onboarding staff to production; implement role bundles and automated deprovisioning.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet established a workforce identity provider or a joiner, mover and leaver process for production. Centralized, automated provisioning and same-day deprovisioning are planned.
residual_risks: Systems that do not support federation require separate deprovisioning and are a common gap.

title: Periodic access recertification and continuous entitlement hygiene
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-004 specifies quarterly recertification for privileged and workforce roles, annual for delegated customer roles, no self-certification, and automatic suspension 14 days after the due date. Not implemented.
target_answer: Access recertification runs quarterly for privileged and workforce roles and at least annually for delegated customer roles (advisors, authorized viewers, agents), and covers third-party authority registers such as bank-portal users and custodian trading authorities. Reviewers cannot certify their own access. Uncertified access is suspended automatically 14 days after the due date and the suspension is recorded and notified. Between reviews, grants carry expiry dates and are revoked by events (termination, role change, death or incapacity, partner exit), so the review confirms a mostly self-cleaning population rather than discovering it. Review evidence includes the complete population with counts reconciled to the system of record.
current_practice: Not implemented. Requirements exist (UNB-XIN-IAM-004, AUTH-I6, CNV-GOV-006).
intended_practice: Implement the recertification campaign engine with automatic suspension and population reconciliation.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design requires quarterly review of privileged and workforce access, annual review of delegated customer roles, no self-certification, and automatic suspension of uncertified access. These are planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Reviewers may approve without scrutiny; automatic suspension only addresses non-response, not careless approval.

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent access creep and catch access that should have been removed.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Former staff, moved staff or departed advisors retain access to funds and data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Periodic manual reviews are widely performed but frequently rubber-stamped; they detect stale access up to a quarter late and depend on reviewer diligence.
challenge.legally_required: NYDFS 500.7 requires covered entities to review access privileges at least annually; PCI DSS 4.0.1 Req 7.2.4 requires reviews at least every six months for in-scope systems. These bind customers or card environments, not Echelon directly.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in bank vendor contracts and SOC 2 control sets (CC6.2, CC6.3).
challenge.historical_convention: Quarterly or semiannual manager attestation campaigns.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Stale access can be largely eliminated by construction: every grant has an expiry and is derived from a parent authority (AUTH-I2), and lifecycle events revoke derived grants automatically (AUTH-I1, UNB-RCN-ENT-004).
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Expiry and event-driven revocation; automatic suspension of uncertified access.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Every grant, expiry and revocation is an append-only event, so the access population at any instant can be reconstructed.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Expiring, event-revoked grants plus a lighter periodic review focused on exceptions and privileged roles.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through the event history and population reconciliation.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Customers and auditors will still expect a periodic review artifact; the by-construction approach is likely accepted as strengthening, not replacing, it.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any grant path that bypasses the authority registry (for example direct database grants or a third-party console).
challenge.alternative_cost: Upfront engineering in the authority model, already required by Unbound design.
challenge.alternative_risks: Over-aggressive expiry can lock out legitimate advisors and create pressure for emergency overrides.
supporting_arguments: Event-driven revocation closes the window between departure and review.
opposing_arguments: Auditors test the review control itself; removing or thinning it may produce findings even if risk is lower.

title: Privileged access to production infrastructure and databases
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-010 requires production database administrative roles to be break-glass only with two-person activation and requires production data access by engineers to follow CNV-ARC-002. UNB-XIN-IAM-001 requires separate principals per realm. CNV-PLT-003 requires AAL3-grade authenticators for privileged roles. None is implemented.
target_answer: There is no standing administrative access to production. Privileged access uses a dedicated PlatformWorkforce principal distinct from any customer or everyday identity, authenticated with AAL3-grade hardware or device-bound keys, elevated just in time for a bounded task with approval by a second person, and recorded in logs that the elevated principal cannot alter. Production database administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation. Application identities hold INSERT and constrained SELECT on authoritative tables and no UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or DDL. The number of people eligible for elevation is published to customers.
intended_practice: Implement just-in-time elevation with two-person approval and immutable session logging before production.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design has no standing production administrative access: privileged access is separately authenticated with hardware-backed keys, time-bound, approved by a second person and logged, and database administrator roles are break-glass only. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Cloud provider root or organization-owner credentials remain a standing privilege that must be sealed separately.
A database administrator with physical storage access can still alter data; the design anchors ledger digests externally (CNV-PLT-010) to detect this, not prevent it.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure that the people with the keys to the kingdom cannot misuse them unnoticed.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Insider fraud, credential theft of an administrator, or ransomware with admin rights.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Commercial privileged access management vaults reduce password exposure but often leave standing eligibility broad and rely on after-the-fact session review that rarely happens.
challenge.legally_required: NYDFS 500.7 (as amended) requires covered entities to limit and periodically review privileged accounts; customers flow this to vendors. Not directly binding on Echelon.
challenge.contractually_required: Common; banks expect PAM and session recording.
challenge.historical_convention: PAM vault, password checkout, session recording.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Standing database write privilege for application identities is eliminated by grant design (INSERT-only on authoritative tables); interactive administration is eliminated except break-glass.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Strata-declared grants with drift detection; elevation tooling that requires a second approver.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Elevation requests, approvals and session logs as append-only events; grant diffs on every deploy.
challenge.stronger_alternative: No standing privilege plus INSERT-only application grants plus external anchoring of ledger digests.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes; grants are inspectable and elevation events are reconstructable.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely, if session recording or equivalent logging of break-glass activity is shown.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If emergency elevation becomes routine, or if cloud console owners can grant themselves database access outside the process.
challenge.alternative_cost: Engineering effort for elevation workflow; possibly lower licensing.
challenge.alternative_risks: Operational friction during incidents may push staff toward workarounds.
supporting_arguments: Removing standing privilege removes the target attackers seek.
opposing_arguments: A small team may lack two qualified people available at all hours for approvals.

title: Break-glass emergency access
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-005 specifies sealed credentials independent of the workforce IdP, two-person activation, four-hour expiry, security owner paging, tenant notification within one hour, and a prohibition on domain transitions. CNV-PLT-007 governs platform-originated holds. Not implemented.
target_answer: Break-glass credentials are sealed and independent of the workforce identity provider, require two-person activation, expire automatically within four hours, page the security owner, and notify affected tenants' administrators within one hour. Break-glass sessions are limited to reading, protective actions (payment freeze, hold, credential revocation) and infrastructure recovery; they cannot approve grants, change payees, change authority, post ledger entries or remove holds. Any authoritative state change without a matching command event blocks affected payments until reviewed. Procedures are tested at least annually without using real customer data.
intended_practice: Implement sealed credential storage, activation workflow and post-use review before production.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design specifies sealed, two-person, time-limited emergency access that notifies affected customers within one hour and cannot change grants, payees, authority or ledger entries. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Two-person activation may be impossible during a severe incident with a very small team; the fallback must be decided in advance.
open_questions: Who are the two people eligible to activate break-glass at launch, given current staffing is not established?

title: Vendor staff access to customer tenant data and access transparency
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-002 and CNV-ARC-002 specify deny-by-default operator access, sponsor pre-approved delegations or per-case approval, prohibition on sponsor decisions, and an access transparency view within 15 minutes. TVR-SEC-007 treats assisted-channel commands as low-assurance. Not implemented.
target_answer: Vendor staff have no access to a customer's non-public data by default. Read diagnostics require an OperatorAccessDelegation pre-approved by the sponsor for listed task classes, scopes and maximum duration; writes require per-case approval by an authorized sponsor approver. Staff cannot perform sponsor decisions (grant approval, payee change, authority change, fund closure) unless the sponsor's delegation names that command class. Revocation takes effect on the next request. Every operator session appears to the customer's administrators within 15 minutes with who, when, scope, reason, case and records touched. Support 'view as' is a distinct low-assurance command kind that cannot add recipients without sponsor-direct confirmation. Support personnel locations and subcontractors are disclosed.
intended_practice: Implement OperatorAccessDelegation, per-case approval and the transparency view as part of the authorization core.
customer_statement: In Echelon's Unbound design, vendor staff cannot access customer data unless the customer pre-approves a scoped, expiring delegation or approves a specific case, and every access is visible to the customer within 15 minutes. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Infrastructure operators with storage-level access can bypass application-level transparency; this is addressed by break-glass rules and encryption, not by the transparency view.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure vendor staff do not browse or alter our clients' data without our knowledge.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Insider snooping, insider fraud, or attacker use of a compromised support account.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional answers ('access is limited to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis, and logged') are unverifiable by the customer and depend on vendor-internal review.
challenge.legally_required: Not specifically; GLBA and Regulation S-P service-provider oversight expectations require the customer to ensure appropriate safeguards.
challenge.contractually_required: Increasingly requested by banks and large enterprises (customer approval of support access, access logs).
challenge.architectural_elimination: Default access is eliminated; access exists only as a customer-approved delegation object.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Authorization core refuses operator requests without an active delegation or case approval (CNV-ARC-002 AC-1, AC-2).
challenge.continuous_evidence: Customer-visible access transparency log generated by the same enforcement path.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Customer-controlled, expiring delegations with customer-visible logs, as specified.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by the customer directly through the transparency view, and by testing denial without a delegation.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any administrative path (database console, log search, backups) that reads tenant data outside the authorization core.
challenge.alternative_cost: Moderate engineering; support latency when approvals are needed.
challenge.alternative_risks: Customers may pre-approve broad delegations for convenience, recreating standing access.
opposing_arguments: Logs and telemetry may still expose data to engineers unless redaction (MON-014) is effective.

title: Service accounts, workload identities and machine credentials
status_rationale: SEC-CRYPTO-001 (proposed) prohibits hardcoded secrets and requires managed keys, secret scanning and rotation. The tenant-aware persistence design grants application identities INSERT and constrained SELECT only. Limen's publishing workflow uses npm Trusted Publishing over GitHub OIDC with no stored npm token, a real example of federated workload identity in Echelon tooling. No production workload identities exist.
target_answer: Every workload (service, job, CI pipeline, agent) has its own identity in the Workload realm, registered in an inventory with owner and purpose. Credentials are short-lived and obtained by workload identity federation (for example OIDC from CI) rather than stored static secrets; any unavoidable static secret is held in a managed secret store and rotated automatically. Workload identities cannot log in interactively. Each component uses a distinct least-privilege database role; no application identity can UPDATE or DELETE authoritative event or journal tables. CI can deploy only artifacts that passed gates and only with approval for control-relevant modules.
current_practice: Not implemented for Unbound. Limen (limen@743cdb9b) publishes its npm package using GitHub OIDC trusted publishing with no stored token, per its README; this is release tooling for an open component, not a production service identity.
intended_practice: Adopt workload identity federation and a secret manager for all Unbound workloads; generate service account inventory from infrastructure code.
provable: The Limen publishing configuration can be shown as an example practice. Nothing for Unbound.
customer_statement: Echelon intends every service and pipeline to use its own short-lived, federated identity with least-privilege database roles and no interactive login. Some Echelon release tooling already publishes without stored tokens; the production design is planned.
residual_risks: Third-party integrations (custodians, banks) may only support static API keys.

title: AI agent identities, authority bounds and suspension
status_rationale: SOC2-017, UNB-XIN-IAM-001 (Workload realm includes AI agent principals), GOV-AUTH-003, GOV-AUTH-024, UNB-AI-STD-001, UNB-AGT-002, UNB-AGT-003 and AIN-013 specify the target. Engineering agents in Echelon repositories are attributed by Praxis using self-declared identity. Nothing is implemented for production.
target_answer: Each product agent is a distinct Workload principal with a named human owner, a declared capability manifest and an authority tier. When an agent acts for a user, it holds a delegated grant derived from that user's authority that can never exceed it and ends when the parent ends; the delegation chain is recorded on every action. Agents cannot grant themselves permissions, approve their own consequential actions, change their own policy or clear their own alerts. Prohibited tools are removed by the tool broker rather than forbidden by prompt. A global and per-tenant emergency stop suspends agents and safely parks queued actions. Engineering agents never hold production customer-data credentials; their CI identity is authenticated workload identity rather than self-declared. Agent identities are included in access reviews and deprovisioned when retired.
current_practice: Requirements only for product agents. Praxis records self-declared engineering-agent identity per execution in development repositories (docs/agent-provenance.md); it is not authenticated.
intended_practice: Implement agent principals, delegation chains, tool broker and emergency stop; bind engineering agent CI runs to authenticated workload identity.
provable: Praxis execution records show declared agent identity for development work; they do not prove identity.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design treats each AI agent as its own bounded, attributable identity that cannot exceed or expand its authority and can be stopped immediately. This is planned. Echelon's development repositories currently record self-declared agent attribution only.
owner: Unassigned; proposed AI Governance owner with Security Lead
residual_risks: Prompt injection can still steer an agent within its granted authority.
Model providers' own staff and systems are outside Echelon's identity controls.

challenge.customer_intent: Make sure AI agents cannot do more than the humans they serve, and that someone can be held responsible.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An agent with shared or excessive credentials moves money, exports data or escalates privilege, with no attributable actor.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional IAM treats agents as service accounts with static broad permissions, which fails to bound per-user authority and enables confused-deputy attacks.
challenge.legally_required: Not specifically regulated in the US for this use; the EU AI Act may impose obligations depending on classification, not established here.
challenge.historical_convention: None; questionnaires are just adding agent identity questions.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Self-escalation can be eliminated by making authority grants a command class agents are never authorized to issue (A5) and enforcing it in the deterministic authorization core.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Delegated grants computed as a subset of the parent; tool broker removes tools; emergency stop as a platform command.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Every agent action carries principal, delegation chain, policy version and tools available.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Per-agent principals with delegation chains and deterministic enforcement, independent of model behavior.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by negative tests (AUTH-T01, AUTH-T08) and inspection of action records.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain; technically strong, but regulated customers have little precedent for evaluating agent identity and may restrict agents to read-only regardless.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If any agent path writes directly to the database (prohibited by GOV-AUTH-023) or reuses a human session token.
challenge.alternative_risks: Complexity in the delegation model may itself contain authorization defects.
supporting_arguments: Deterministic enforcement does not depend on the model behaving.
Delegation chains preserve accountability to a human.
opposing_arguments: Prompt injection operates within granted authority, so bounding authority does not prevent misuse of what is granted.
No independent standard yet exists for auditors to test against.

title: Customer administrator delegation and customer-side user management
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-001 defines realms including SponsorWorkforce and PartnerWorkforce; UNB-TEN-010 states partner preferences cannot override sponsor reserved authority; CNV-GOV-006 requires delegated customer roles to expire on events with risk-based recertification; GOV-AUTH-015 requires expiring, revocable delegation. Not implemented.
target_answer: Sponsor administrators manage their own users within the SponsorWorkforce realm and may delegate administration of defined scopes (program, partner, function) to sub-administrators. No administrator can grant a permission they do not hold or assign sponsor-reserved authority. Distribution-partner administrators manage only PartnerWorkforce users for their partner and cannot administer sponsor-reserved functions. Changes to administrator roles require step-up authentication and, for the top administrative tier, a second sponsor approver. Delegated roles expire and are recertified. If a customer loses all administrators, recovery requires verified authorization from the customer's designated officers through an out-of-band, identity-proofed procedure with a waiting period and notification to all prior administrators; vendor staff cannot grant administrative rights on their own.
intended_practice: Implement delegated administration with subset-only grants and an administrator recovery procedure.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design lets sponsors manage and delegate their own administration, prevents any administrator from granting more than they hold, separates partner administration from sponsor-reserved functions, and requires a verified customer-authorized procedure to recover lost administrator access. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Administrator recovery is a social-engineering target; the procedure's strength depends on the identity proofing of customer officers.
open_questions: What artifact proves that a person is an authorized officer of a sponsor for administrator recovery (board resolution, signatory list)?

title: Identity lifecycle for donors, advisors and partner-federated users
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-003 (risk-based proofing, no KBA), UNB-XIN-IAM-001 (one realm per principal; separate principals per sponsor), UNB-RCN-ENT-004 (suspend rights and agents on death or incapacity in one transaction), AUTH-I5 (unauthenticated death notice is a flag), UNB-XIN-SAS-007 (sponsor-direct credential before partner federation ends) specify the target. Not implemented.
target_answer: Donors and advisors are identity-proofed by a risk-based process that validates core attributes against authoritative sources, matches the funding account owner, and steps up to document verification or a non-biometric alternative when needed; knowledge-based questions are never used for proofing. Each person has one principal per sponsor and per realm; a staff member who is also a donor has two principals linked only by an audited link that confers no privilege. On verified death or incapacity, all rights, sessions and delegated agent principals derived from that person are suspended in one transaction; an unverified notice only holds new actions. Users federated through a distribution partner are offered a sponsor-direct authenticator at first login so they keep access to their funds if the partner relationship ends.
intended_practice: Implement realms, proofing workflow, lifecycle events and sponsor-direct enrollment.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design proofs donor and advisor identities without knowledge-based questions, keeps roles and sponsors in separate identities, suspends all derived access at verified death or incapacity, and keeps donors' access to their funds if a distribution partner exits. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Identity proofing vendors introduce their own data handling and accuracy risks.
Synthetic identities can pass attribute validation.
